items.title: WHILE YOU SLEPT, ONE MODEL SPENT 10 DAYS BREAKING LINUX AND FOUND 948 DOORS TO ROOT.
items.summary:
WHILE YOU SLEPT, ONE MODEL SPENT 10 DAYS BREAKING LINUX AND FOUND 948 DOORS TO ROOT.

not a hacker group. not a state. a pipeline of OpenAI agents running on $1.2M of API

that kernel runs your server, your Android and the cloud. and it wrote a patch for every door    
           
GPT-6 Cyber is a separate model trained to find bugs and write working exploits. i went through the 27-min report, here's the line stage by stage

▹ what runs under the hood

1. SCOUT agents: 5,034 audit targets · 2.8M lines · 7% of the kernel · $3,426

2. ANALYST agents: 2,308 candidate findings in 12h · $316,549

3. TRIAGE agents: PoC in a KASAN VM, retry until it crashes · 1,724 reproduced in 30h · 74.7% hit rate · only 3.1% wrong analysis

4. EXPLOITDEV agents: SMEP · SMAP · KASLR on, stock distro · 1,169 working root shells · 948 distinct bugs · $1,279 per bug

5. PATCH agents: a patch for every bug · 304 critical sent to maintainers first · humans review before anything ships

6. same harness, new brain: GPT-5.6 Sol in july → 166 · GPT-6 Cyber in october → 948 · 5.7x

SCOUT → ANALYST → TRIAGE → SCREEN → EXPLOITDEV → PATCH → HUMAN

firefox: 81 new high-severity bugs. Mozilla already shipping fixes (MFSA 2026-118). Mozilla and Palo Alto Networks are on Cyber already

cost: $1.2M in API for one run. at Pwn2Own / TyphoonPWN prices those 948 exploits are worth $18.9M–$66.3M

access: no public release. GPT-6 Cyber goes to approved orgs via Daybreak Red, behind an IP allowlist. defenders get GPT-6 Astra via Daybreak Blue. everyone else: plain Astra

▹ the edge

alone each agent is mid. together they're a loop: find → prove → break → fix, and you rerun it on every new model

OpenAI own line: a low-privilege account on an unpatched box = root for a well-funded attacker. bot, hot wallet or validator key on a linux server you haven't updated? that's your threat model now

10 days after the scan: 61 fixes upstream · 43 staging · 299 discussed in public. the patch race already started

will models fix the internet faster than they break it?

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

args.text:
Nguyên hàm (tích phân bất định) của $x^2$ là:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

**Lời giải chi tiết:**
- Sử dụng công thức nguyên hàm cơ bản của hàm số mũ: 
  $$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (với \ n \neq -1)$$
- Thay $n = 2$ vào công thức:
  $$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

*(Trong đó $C$ là hằng số tích phân tùy ý).*

# Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence

Intelligence in machines

"AI" redirects here. For other uses, see [AI (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_(disambiguation) "AI (disambiguation)") and [Artificial intelligence (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_(disambiguation) "Artificial intelligence (disambiguation)").

**Artificial intelligence** ( **AI**) is the capability of [computational systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer "Computer") to perform tasks typically associated with [human intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_intelligence "Human intelligence"), such as [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning "Learning"), [reasoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reason "Reason"), [problem-solving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem-solving "Problem-solving"), [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception "Perception"), and [decision-making](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision-making "Decision-making"). It is also a field of research spanning [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science"), [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering "Engineering"), and [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") that develops and studies methods and [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software") enabling machines to perceive their environment and use [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence "Intelligence") to take actions that maximise their chances of achieving defined goals.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211%E2%80%934-1)

Prominent [applications of AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence "Applications of artificial intelligence") include advanced [web search engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_search_engine "Web search engine"), [chatbots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot "Chatbot"), [virtual assistants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant "Virtual assistant"), [autonomous vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_vehicles "Autonomous vehicles"), play and analysis in [strategy games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_game "Strategy game") (e.g., [chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess "Chess") and [Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(game) "Go (game)")), and [content generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") (e.g., text, images, audio, and videos).

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. items.title: From scans to scribes, Yale medical faculty talk AI use in healthcare | Yale Daily News
items.summary:
Normally, diagnosing prostate cancer includes a blood test, MRI imaging and a formal diagnosis from a radiologist, who might read the same MRI image differently on different days.

Now, Onofrey said, he and other researchers are training deep learning models on these images to look for diseases including prostate cancer, though he said researchers have not validated models in large enough settings for clinical adoption yet. [...] Technology companies will face skepticism, according to Papademetris. Many AI models remain “black box” models, meaning users do not know the details of the inner workings behind the AI used in practice.

Though scientific advancement is exciting, Papademetris cautioned about implementing AI into healthcare without the proper guardrails in place. [...] Some provider systems, such as Yale Health, have incorporated AI scribes to help draft notes from patient visits. Yale researchers and professors spoke to the News about their experiences with AI-powered tools. Xenophon Papademetris, a professor at the School of Medicine, said people should be skeptical of AI use in everyday clinical practice.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] In October, several states sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gives dangerous medical advice and misleads consumers about safety. OpenAI says it will continue to improve the model. [...] We are not proposing a new regulatory regime, which may not be needed. The insurance industry’s crash tests have spurred automakers to build safer vehicles, beyond what federal rules require. AI companies could publish behavioral test results, letting hospitals, health insurers, and consumers choose accordingly.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
